title: A 4 GB Laptop GPU Beats a 12-Core CPU by 4.3x on Gemma 4
why_read: A concrete, controlled benchmark comparing CPU versus a modest laptop GPU for local LLM inference gives useful real-world numbers for people running small models on consumer hardware.
analysis: The article compares running a small Gemma model quantized to 4-bit through llama.cpp on the same laptop, once purely on CPU and once offloaded to a 4GB GTX 1650 Ti GPU, changing only a single command-line flag. It reports a 4.3x decode speed improvement on the GPU while using only about 1.6GB of VRAM, with byte-identical inputs and binaries across both runs to ensure a fair comparison. This kind of controlled, apples-to-apples local benchmark is genuinely useful for people deciding whether a budget GPU is worth using for local LLM inference. The methodology, keeping everything constant except one flag, makes the result more trustworthy than typical vague benchmark claims.
